ai.definition: Autonomous construction-site robots are self-driving machines designed to perform tasks such as grading, excavating, and laying out floor plans on job sites with minimal human supervision.
ai.howItWorks: These robots use GPS, LiDAR (Light Detection and Ranging) sensors, and site models to follow a pre-programmed plan. Layout robots can print reference lines directly from the design using precise positioning systems.
ai.problemSolved: They address the need for efficient, accurate, and cost-effective construction of infrastructure projects by reducing human labor intensity and improving precision in earthworks and site layout tasks.
ai.manufacturing: Manufacturing involves assembling components such as autonomous navigation systems, sensors (GPS and LiDAR), and robotic arms or tracks. These are integrated with software that controls the robot's movements and operations based on predefined plans.
ai.buildProcess: The build process includes designing the hardware to ensure it can handle heavy loads and harsh environments, programming the software for autonomous operation, and testing in controlled settings before deployment on actual construction sites.
ai.costDrivers: Cost drivers include the initial investment in advanced sensors and navigation systems, ongoing maintenance of these technologies, and the need for skilled personnel to operate and maintain the robots. Additionally, there are costs associated with integrating the technology into existing workflows.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The outlook is positive as the technology shows promise in improving efficiency and safety on construction sites, but it requires further refinement and standardization to become widely adopted.
ai.regulation: There are currently no specific regulations for autonomous construction-site robots. However, there may be future requirements related to safety standards, data privacy, and interoperability with existing construction equipment.
ai.risks: Risks include technical challenges such as ensuring reliable operation in varying weather conditions, potential cybersecurity threats, and the risk of accidents during integration or use. There are also concerns about job displacement for human workers.
ai.profitability: Profitability is uncertain due to high initial costs and the need for significant investment in infrastructure and workforce training. However, long-term savings from increased efficiency could lead to profitability over time.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future development will likely focus on improving autonomy levels, enhancing precision, and expanding the range of tasks that can be performed autonomously. Integration with other technologies like drones and IoT systems is also expected.

glossary.def: Capable of performing tasks independently without continuous human intervention.

subsystems.name: Perception
subsystems.role: senses the terrain, obstacles, people and other machines around the vehicle.

subsystems.name: Localisation
subsystems.role: works out where the machine is and how it is oriented, to centimetre accuracy.

subsystems.name: Machine control
subsystems.role: turns planned motions into precise movement of the bucket, blade or arm.

subsystems.name: Site model and task planner
subsystems.role: holds the digital design and decides what to dig, grade or mark out next.

subsystems.name: Safety and supervision
subsystems.role: keeps people out of harm's way and lets a human monitor or take over.

subsystems.name: Power and drivetrain
subsystems.role: provides the energy and traction to move and work.

buildSteps.title: Create the digital site model
buildSteps.detail: Drone or ground surveys build a 3D terrain model, which is merged with the design file (BIM) to define target surfaces and volumes.

buildSteps.title: Prepare the machine
buildSteps.detail: A conventional excavator, dozer or skid-steer is either retrofitted or built new with electrohydraulic controls, a control computer and mounting points for sensors.

buildSteps.title: Fit and calibrate sensors
buildSteps.detail: GNSS antennas, lidar, cameras and an inertial unit are mounted rigidly and calibrated so their measurements agree with the machine's own geometry.

buildSteps.title: Teach or program the task
buildSteps.detail: An operator either demonstrates the motion, or the planner computes cut-and-fill passes directly from the site model.

buildSteps.title: Run in supervised autonomy
buildSteps.detail: The machine executes the plan at low speed inside a fenced or empty area, with a human ready to hit the emergency stop.

buildSteps.title: Add perception and obstacle avoidance
buildSteps.detail: Software is tuned so the machine stops for people, vehicles or unexpected obstacles, and resumes when the path is clear.

buildSteps.title: Scale to a working site
buildSteps.detail: Multiple machines are coordinated, and a single remote supervisor oversees a fleet while other trades work nearby.

buildSteps.title: Validate and certify
buildSteps.detail: The system is tested against safety standards and site rules, and its behaviour is logged for every autonomous action.

prerequisites.tech: Safety standards and regulation for autonomous heavy equipment
prerequisites.why: rules for driverless machines on shared construction sites are still developing.

pathway.milestone: auto-grade and auto-stop features on excavators and dozers
pathway.unlocks: faster, more accurate earthworks with an operator still in the cab.

pathway.milestone: fully autonomous earthmoving on fenced or segregated sites
pathway.unlocks: repetitive groundwork without a driver, especially in remote or hazardous areas.

pathway.milestone: supervised fleets of several machines working together
pathway.unlocks: one operator overseeing many machines, cutting labour per cubic metre moved.

pathway.milestone: integrated autonomous site with layout, excavation and lifting robots sharing one model
pathway.unlocks: round-the-clock construction with fewer people in dangerous zones.
